limitations.summary: No production authentication, authorization, RLS or ABAC enforcement is implemented.
Environment-referenced source values exist, but the validated defaults/TOML/env/secret-store configuration model is not implemented.

Owned serving SQLite cancels its pre-worker admission wait and interrupts active VM work after mutex acquisition. It does not pre-empt raw standard-mutex wait, already-submitted/running blocking work, busy timeout, blocking UDF/VFS/I/O, detached compiler CPU, raw/conformance work, or establish common database-native statement cancellation.
DESCRIBE has compiler-only tests but no end-to-end backend or endpoint result evidence.
Snapshot-local source identity exists, but there is no registry, coordinator or multi-source production caller.

A finite root variable-key ORDER window has stable bounded compaction, an explicit row ceiling and retained textual-payload accounting, but fresh-process RSS and independent semantic-oracle qualification remain open; expression ORDER fails closed. GROUP, solution/term DISTINCT and graph-dedup bounded physical implementations remain unavailable.
The parser feature recognizes LATERAL, but both compiler paths reject it and no execution profile is implemented.
The PostgreSQL/MySQL evidence can skip on provider absence and therefore cannot establish production admission.
Live result-column probes and branch emission fail closed before cursor I/O, but the sequential preflight can race later DDL and is not a coherent schema-generation lease.
No sealed W3C RDB2RDF mapping execution matrix exists for MySQL.
The MySQL source-selector branch lacks a positive open_backend selector test.
Production telemetry, health/readiness endpoints, graceful shutdown and the complete lifecycle control plane remain unimplemented.
Recursive property paths use an exact finite-pair fixed point, but total work/cancellation budgets and live PostgreSQL/MySQL qualification remain open.

Compiler-only no-primary-key path SQL maps the synthetic `rowid` sentinel to snapshot-local PostgreSQL `ctid`; a real `rowid` column still collides and live PostgreSQL path execution is not evidenced.
Mutable product-mock PostgreSQL is an optional development differential. Its table/column inventory currently rejects drift and grants no backend admission.
The complete backend contract, live matrix, security, cancellation and conformance gates in ADR-0038 R3 are incomplete.

No pinned SPARQL Protocol manifest is executed; the tested read-only HTTP subset accepts exactly one query parameter for GET/form POST or one raw query body, rejects dataset/version/extra parameters, and is not full Protocol conformance.

The serving lane shares one absolute deadline and finite ceilings for observable metadata probes, branch opens, pull attempts, semantic result items, serializer writes and ORDER textual-payload high-water growth; an independent row window bounds fixed per-row ORDER overhead. These are not a total heap ceiling. Compiler CPU, database rows scanned, recursive SQL iterations/source cost, raw/conformance callers, common source-native statement cancellation and atomic/no-prefix post-200 responses remain outside total M2 QueryBudget.

Narrow private diagnostics include same-byte static RootPie preflight, a counterfactual non-authority bubblewrap name/path inventory, and late seccomp; actual host byte consumption/runtime closure, the minimal production dependency closure, and exact-artifact release proof are not implemented.

Explicit-R2RML serving quarantines unverified constraints and type-authorized pooling, while live result-column preflight fails closed; coherent structural/type generations, typed synthetic row identity, atomic reload, verified optimisation and Direct Mapping regeneration remain unimplemented.

Canonical semantic-builder gold and the sealed semantic-product-mock source are development authorities. The in-charter slice maps one table and proves neither image/source provenance nor backend admission.

Immutable request leases and a private checked publication primitive exist, but validated candidate construction, automatic drift observation/revision, verified backend-generation leases and public reload/health are not implemented.

SQLite serving admission caps active leased work per physical connection and each waiter is deadline/cancellation-bound. Raw pool/mutex users bypass it, round-robin is not availability-aware, and the standard mutex plus submitted/running blocking work remain non-cancellable.
Post-200 SELECT/CONSTRUCT failures terminate the body and may expose a usable prefix; they cannot become RFC 9457 responses.
Remote-source TLS verification and a production secret-store transport remain unimplemented.

cells.qualification: Tower Service::call mints one deadline after HTTP/request-target parsing and before Axum route/method dispatch; it governs serve-layer async waiters and bounded producer checkpoints, not cooperative CPU/native cancellation, total QueryBudget or atomic post-200 streaming.

One shared finite fail-fast gate (default 64, checked from 1 through Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS) bounds requests admitted into application work. Saturation in Service::call returns a distinct redacted 503 service-overloaded response with Retry-After: 1 before Router or request-body polling; deadline/control failures take precedence and a closed gate is an internal 500. One RequestBudget retains capacity through active streaming producers and queued/running compiler or SQLite workers after waiter timeout or drop, but releases it after active work ends even while already-produced bounded response bytes remain unread. Required tests use virtual time and explicit barriers. This is admitted application work, not total TCP connections, sockets, responses, a rate limit, fairness, native-work pre-emption, total QueryBudget, production source admission, or atomic post-200 delivery. A shed unpolled POST body can affect HTTP/1 connection reuse or reset behaviour.

Required strict-subset tests accept exactly one query for GET or form POST, or one raw POST body. Raw bodies have a per-request n-byte cap; form bodies have a checked per-request 3n+16 wire cap and n-byte decoded-query cap. Optional version, dataset, duplicate and extra parameters reject instead of being ignored; unsupported media rejects without polling the application body. This is not full Protocol conformance.

One Rust state owns an immutable source-keyed runtime snapshot. Each ready request loads and pins exactly one generation before body polling through EOF, error, cancellation or drop; new requests see a complete successor or a redacted not-ready response. Monotonic IDs, complete expected-readiness comparison, destructor release outside the lock and deterministic stale/slow/drift races are required evidence. Publication is crate-private and non-authorizing: no validated candidate builder, automatic watcher, repeated-NotReady revision, verified backend lease, public reload/health surface, Direct Mapping lifecycle or source admission is claimed.

Probes are sequential and non-atomic; bounded lexical alias folding remains only for offline/synthetic emission and translate-time immediate wrappers, never live metadata authority. This is defense in depth, not drift detection or a generation lease.

One serving identity begins in Tower Service::call after HTTP/request-target parsing and before Axum route/method dispatch, then spans strict request admission, compiler and pool waits, the controlled executor, handler handoff and serialization with inclusive observable source/result/serialized-byte and ORDER retained-payload ceilings. Closed classification rejects source-sized Rust fallback states before backend selection or I/O. A finite root variable-key ORDER window is the one implemented exception: stable compaction retains at most OFFSET+LIMIT rows between fixed reconstruction batches, row and textual-payload ceilings are independent, LIMIT 0 performs no source I/O, and a 10x-to-100x heap smoke passes the programme's 10% gate. Only the owned serving SQLite path interrupts active VM work after acquiring its connection mutex. It shares the request control identity, records the local cause before interruption, removes its exclusively owned progress handler before reuse and leaves unrelated SQLITE_INTERRUPT failures as driver errors. The separate serving admission gate precedes worker submission, but raw standard-mutex wait and already-submitted/running blocking work, busy timeout, blocking UDF/VFS/I/O, compiler CPU, raw/conformance callers, PostgreSQL/MySQL, database rows or recursive source work, total M2, production admission, and atomic post-200 delivery remain outside this profile.

Each physical pool member has one permanent cap-one serving admission identity. SELECT, ASK and CONSTRUCT await the selected member under the same RequestBudget before any SQLite blocking worker is submitted; timeout or cancellation removes that waiter, and an admission timeout returns pre-200 504 without SQLite entry. The public lease is non-Clone and consumed once; private state is retained/cloned into column_names and open_branch workers through exit, preventing early capacity return. Active leases, each waiter's lifetime and aggregate admitted application work are bounded. Raw SqlitePool::pick and foreign mutex holders bypass admission; the standard mutex and submitted/running blocking work remain non-cancellable; busy/UDF/VFS/I/O stay non-preemptible; selection is round-robin rather than availability-aware. This is not total M2, another backend, compiler/raw/conformance/database-row/recursive-work/post-200 atomicity, or production admission.

Compiler CPU, database rows scanned, recursive SQL/source cost, raw/conformance callers, common source-native statement cancellation and atomic/no-prefix post-200 responses are not claimed.

SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL source selectors feed one immutable source/backend/compiler/cache binding inside a source-keyed runtime snapshot; reachability is not admission. Ready requests pin one application generation through response termination, and the checked publication primitive swaps whole snapshots without mixing generations, but it remains crate-private and non-authorizing. PostgreSQL introspection and unqualified base-table resolution are `public`-scoped and fail on schema/catalogue identity ambiguity. Explicit-R2RML serving quarantines unverified integrity constraints and prevents mutable startup types from authorizing cross-column PostgreSQL pooling. Every recursively reachable base Table/Query source is probed and its referenced columns fail closed before cursor I/O, including base-source references inside nested emission. Offline/synthetic alias folding and translate-time immediate wrappers retain a bounded non-SQL-token-aware heuristic, never live metadata authority. Shared term-dedup captures the complete BGP key, including an active graph variable, before projection, crosses only physically key-preserving pure unary wrappers, is revalidated before metadata I/O, and overlays only a private execution clone; unsafe scopes return `501`. Fully ground overlap uses an exact SQL unit-relation pool, and serving rejects the remaining source-sized fallback pre-I/O. Trusted raw `rr:sqlQuery` is not schema-confined, while TOCTOU-safe structural/type generations, typed row identity, validated candidate construction, automatic drift/reload, verified backend leases and Direct Mapping lifecycle remain open.

The Rust serving path now owns one source-keyed immutable runtime snapshot and pins one ready generation per request through response EOF, error, cancellation or drop. Checked monotonic publication rejects stale, slow and ready-to-not-ready races and releases old resources only after the last lease. The primitive is crate-private and non-authorizing; validated candidate construction, automatic drift/reload, repeated-not-ready revision fencing, verified backend leases, public lifecycle endpoints, Direct Mapping and source admission remain open.

The in-repo required tests lock a verifier for 139 canonical semantic-builder gold artifacts and 171 files from exact semantic-product-mock revision 7c45292fccb8b88afe263e18de6806667ae18573; the exact external KAT is diagnostic because CI supplies neither root. Generated .metaharness copies are evidence only, and this static contract proves neither mutable PostgreSQL state, image/source provenance nor production admission.
External SERVICE and named non-enabled source forms are rejected before query execution or connector construction.

Credential-bearing PostgreSQL/MySQL source specifications can be supplied through a bounded environment reference; parsed inline passwords fail before runtime, file or network I/O. TLS, layered configuration, telemetry and external secret-store integration remain open.

Serving rejects known source-sized Rust fallback plans before backend selection or source I/O. It admits only finite root variable-key ORDER windows within independent row and retained textual-payload ceilings; LIMIT 0 performs no source I/O, while expression, overflow, unbounded and nested ORDER fail closed. A 10x-to-100x heap smoke passes, but fresh-process RSS and an independent semantic oracle remain required before M1 qualification. Top-level ordered ASK needs no global sort buffer; GROUP and dedup fallbacks still reject.

The owned serving SQLite path has required evidence for query-local interruption of active VM work after mutex acquisition, exact local-cause preservation, handler cleanup and connection reuse. Its separate serving admission gate does not make raw standard-mutex wait or submitted/running blocking work cancellable; busy/UDF/VFS/I/O, compiler, raw/conformance, PostgreSQL/MySQL, database/recursive work, total M2, production admission and atomic post-200 delivery remain outside this narrow profile.

Owned serving SQLite has required proof of one permanent cap-one admission identity per physical pool member. SELECT/ASK/CONSTRUCT wait under the same RequestBudget before blocking-worker submission; admission timeout/cancellation leaves the wait, timeout is pre-200 504 without SQLite entry, and private lease state is retained/cloned into metadata/row workers through exit. The public lease is non-Clone and consumed once. Active leases, per-waiter lifetime and aggregate admitted application work are bounded. Raw pick/foreign holders bypass the gate; the standard mutex and submitted/running work remain non-cancellable; busy/UDF/VFS/I/O, availability-aware selection, other backends, compiler/raw/conformance/database-row/recursive work, total M2, post-200 atomicity and production admission remain open.

SQLite has required evidence for a strict read-only endpoint subset: exactly one query in GET/form POST or one raw POST body; raw per-request cap n, checked form wire cap 3n+16 and decoded cap n; optional version/dataset/extra parameters rejected instead of ignored; unsupported media rejected without application-body polling; ASK JSON, SELECT JSON/XML/CSV/TSV and CONSTRUCT Turtle/N-Triples/JSON-LD. Full Protocol remains open.
The simple SQLite streaming-CONSTRUCT profile has a required growing-source constant-memory benchmark; this does not cover global operators.
